posts.body:
I'm using a certain line of code to make enemies move to a specific point on the map. It works fine with just one, but problems arise once I add a second enemy. Once one enemy reaches its specific map point, the other stops. I don't know much about Javascript, so I can't be 100% certain as to why this is happening. However, my guess is that since both lines of code are basically the same, it's using the same variable in some place. (Might not make much sense, but again, my Javascript knowledge is limited.
Below is the line of code I'm using for one of the enemies. (The other is the exact same except for the cords). I'm hoping someone could help me understand this code and how to make it work.
JavaScript:
var d = this.findDirectionTo(9, 9); if (!d || !this.canPass(this.x, this.y, d)) { this.forceMoveRoute({ list: [{ code: 0 }] }); this.setMovementSuccess(true); this._moveRouteIndex--; } else this.moveStraight(d);

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Okay, that barely qualifies as "a line of code". Here it is properly laid out:
JavaScript:
var d = this.findDirectionTo(9, 9);
if(!d || !this.canPass(this.x, this.y, d)) {
    this.forceMoveRoute({ list: [{ code: 0 }] });
    this.setMovementSuccess(true);
    this._moveRouteIndex--;
} else this.moveStraight(d);
Your guess is wrong – there's no common variable being used there that would interfere across two different events.
So, let's see. What it does is:
Run the A* pathfinder to determine the next hop on the best path to (9,9).
If there is a route to that path, and the direction is passable, move in that direction (the "else" branch). But, in fact, the
canPass
call is redundant, as
findDirectionTo
is already checking passability. So you could simplify it to just
if(!d)
If there is no route to that path (
findDirection
returned 0), you're doing something weird:
The
forceMoveRoute
call is equivalent to a Set Movement Route command with all 3 checkboxes unticked and no move commands. In other words: setting a blank movement route that does not loop, does not skip if it can't move, and does not wait for completion.
Then you're making the move route consider the current move to be a success. That doesn't really make sense, since you just overrode your move route with a new one.
Finally, you're decrementing the move route index… but it's already 0, so now you're making it negative?
Keeping all that in mind, I think your code can be simplified to just this:
JavaScript:
var d = this.findDirectionTo(9, 9);
if(d) this.moveStraight(d);
Though I could be missing something.
That might fix the issue already, as you mentioned that the problem occurred when one enemy reached its destination. In other words, it occurred when
findDirectionTo
returned 0 because the enemy was already on the target location, which thus triggered it to do that weird move route override thing. Since the simplified code doesn't do that, it might be enough to fix your issue. But, since it doesn't do that, it might end up creating a different issue instead.
Let me know how it goes.

This is related to the move route index (
advanceMoveRouteIndex
). In MV there is still a bug where the index skips a step after being restored.
This has been fixed in MZ
by marking
processRouteEnd
as an unsuccessful move command if the route is neither autonomous nor repeating. For repeating routes, index is instead reset to -1 on route end (and then gets incremented to 0 right afterwards), hence the index decrement.
To work the same in all versions of MV/Z the movement should be marked successful and the index manually decremented to compensate. Thus the current "Path to Tile" script call in
the spreadsheet
(currently row 757).

if(!d) {
this._moveRoute.repeat = false;
Click to expand...

Click to expand...
OK, let's have a closer look at your event:
You're using a plugin to turn on/off a switch named "Sight test", right?
When sight is established, the "Chase test" switch is turned on.
The "Timer" variable gets +1 every frame the enemy is chasing but can't see the player.
When "Timer" is
exactly
300, the enemy starts walking home.
Once they're home, the "Chase test" switch is turned off.
Seems sensible! Now, a thought experiment: what if there are other enemies sharing those values?
"Sight test" switch:
OK if the switch is toggled per-event, immediately before running event commands. (I think this is likely.)
Conflicts if the switch is toggled at a different time.
To check the timing we'd need to know which plugin it is (you can link to the plugin's page/thread).
"Chase test" switch:
All enemies start
and stop
chasing at the same time.
I.e. when
any
enemy gets back home,
all
enemies resume their original, non-chasing behaviour.
"Timer" variable:
Advances faster with more enemies, since each enemy event gives +1 to the timer.
May exceed 300, breaking the "= 300" check:
Enemy #1 will start going home;
The others will
keep chasing
until that guy is home;
Once enemy #1 is home, all enemies will reset at the same time.
I guess you can see the problem now!
I'm not sure what the best solution might be, with the plugin you're using. To track "going home" separately for each enemy, I'd consider using a range of switches (or just e.g. self-switch A on each enemy). E.g. turn on each enemy's "go home" switch, then turn off the "chase" switch. Each enemy could then have pages like:
Original behaviour (no conditions):
(Does whatever that enemy does.)
Going home (condition = self-switch A is ON):
Set Movement Route: {Script: etc} (Wait, Repeat)
Turn off self-switch A.
Chasing (condition = switch Chase is ON):
(Chase stuff.)
Note that if you want to use self-switches for this then you'll need a script call (to toggle a different event's self-switch), e.g.
JavaScript:
// Turn on self-switch A for event ID 2 on this map.
$gameSelfSwitches.setValue([this._mapId, 2, "A"], true);
You could also consider moving the timer/"end chase" control to a new Parallel event to avoid counting multiple times per frame. Again, the actual implementation would depend on what the plugin you're using offers for sight checks. If necessary you could add another switch, e.g.
Each enemy event:
If (this enemy can see the player):
Turn on switch "Player Spotted".
Timer event:
If switch "Player Spotted" is ON:
Timer = 0
Else:
Timer += 1
If Timer = 300: (end chase)
Turn off switch "Player Spotted".
Hopefully that helps~

Oh, huh. All right then, I'll close it for you.
This thread is being closed, per OP's request. If for some reason you would like this thread re-opened, please report this post and leave a message why. Thank you.
Just click the "⚠Report" button at the bottom of this post if you change your mind~
For reference, the next thing I'd've asked for would be:
New screenshots of your event pages, and
Screenshot(s) of your Plugin Manager showing all plugins you're using and their load order.
It's possible that there's a mistake/oversight in my suggestions, your implementation, or both...or that you're simply using conflicting plugins. E.g. a plugin for pixel- and/or 8-directional-movement might not work as anticipated with 4-directional tile-based pathfinding.
